title: Pool sizing + negotiation anchors (1:1 prep)
body:
Context / purpose:
- Prep notes for 1:1 with Ravi (infra finance + procurement) on committed GPU ask for Q2–Q3 and a short-term burst plan.
- Aim: get alignment on a two-part agreement: (1) a baseline commit for predictable throughput, (2) negotiated burst credits at a higher spot price for busy days.

Top-level ask (what I want from Ravi):
- Baseline: 40x A100 equivalent (or 80x 80GB-quant-equivalent) committed for 12 months, bill-smoothing option, with a quarterly review trigger.
- Burst pool: 20% of baseline available as on-demand credits with preapproved spend cap = $80k/month.
- SLA uplift (priority routing) for Dedicated tenants when on baseline capacity.

Why: quick bullets for 1:1
- Predictability: committing avoids expensive spot churn during enterprise demos/blackout windows.
- Unit economics: baseline commit + quantization pipeline reduces per-token cost 18–23% vs pure on-demand.
- Ops friction: fewer emergency scale-ups -> less SRE paging and faster mean time to recovery.

Assumptions / back-of-envelope numbers (call these out as negotiable):
- Avg token throughput: 1.2B tokens/day across hosted + dedicated loads (current mixed traffic).
- 1 A100 equivalent can sustain ~2.4M tokens/hour at p95 under our batching profile -> ~57.6M tokens/day.
- Baseline units needed = ceil(1.2B / 57.6M) ≈ 21 -> apply 2.0x safety/variance factor for real ops -> ~42 GPUs. Round to 40 for negotiation simplicity.
- Cost assumptions: committed unit price (internal target) = $6k/GPU-month; on-demand equivalent = $10k/GPU-month; burst premium = +40% over committed rate.
- Monthly baseline cost estimate = 40 * $6k = $240k.
- Worst-case on-demand for same capacity = 40 * $10k = $400k -> leverage this delta in talking with finance.

Operational constraints and asks for the contract language (things to push for):
- Guaranteed minimum baseline reservable in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 (we need cross-region failover).
- Option to add short-duration seats (24–72h) at a fixed burst rate without long procurement.
- Ability to change device class (A100 <-> H100-equivalent) with 30d notice for major upgrades.
- Credit rollover of unused burst credits for up to one month.

Decision tradeoffs to surface in the 1:1:
- Safety factor 2.0 vs 1.5: ops prefers 2.0 for headroom; finance will push lower. Suggest compromise: start at 1.75 for Q2 with a 30-day revisit.
- Commit length 12 vs 24 months: longer gives more discount; shorter keeps flexibility for model migration. I prefer 12 + option to extend at pre-agreed price.
- Burst pool size: fixed % vs dynamic on-demand cap. Recommend fixed % for predictability, but allow auto-burst with cost guardrails.

Negotiation anchors (phrasing to use):
- "Predictability premium": "We can accept a modest discount in exchange for 12-month committed capacity because it materially reduces ops overhead and on-call volume; that value should be reflected in the unit price."
- "Operational safety buffer": "We need a defined headroom guarantee — not just best-effort capacity. Can we contract a 20% reserved failover pool?"
- "Upgrade path": "As models evolve, device mix changes. Let's include a migration clause with 30-day notice and proportional pricing adjustments."

Short checklist for the meeting (carry + ask):
- Bring the traffic histogram from Feb (p50/p95/p99) — show spike days and where we fell over.
- Show MR of autoscale change that reduced cold-starts (PR 812).
- Request finance to provide a floor committed price and an on-demand ceiling so we can model risk.
- Ask procurement for SLA wording sample for cross-region priority routing.

Quick talk-track for Ravi (2–3 min):
- Start: "We need a baseline we can rely on for customer SLAs. We propose a 40-GPU baseline for Q2 with a compact burst credit program to handle marketing demos and unpredictable spikes."
- Middle: show cost delta and the ops cost reduction thesis (fewer emergency purchases, fewer pages).
- Close: "If we agree to 12 months, we need a simple option to scale regionally and a migration clause for new device classes."

Action items (who does what, target dates)
- Aisha: prepare Feb traffic histogram + p95 spike day examples. Due: 2026-03-04.
- Marco: run alternative safety-factor sims (1.5 / 1.75 / 2.0) and produce cost tables. Upload to GH gist. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Elena: draft suggested SLA contract snippets (cross-region, headroom guarantee, burst-credit rollover). Due: 2026-03-06.
- Ravi (finance): provide committed-unit floor and an on-demand ceiling numbers for negotiation. Due: 2026-03-09.

Open questions to surface / things to confirm in meeting:
- Can procurement sign off on 30-day device-class migration without re-negotiating pricing?
- Is there a billing mechanism for instantaneous burst charges (invoices vs monthly reconciliation)?
- Does finance require a minimum spend threshold to trigger the committed discount? If so, where is the trigger?

Fallbacks if baseline can't be secured:
- Option A: negotiate a shorter baseline (90 days) with higher unit discount and quarterly renewals.
- Option B: keep on-demand but implement proactive throttling and pre-warm hooks for highest-priority paths.
- Option C: move critical customers to Dedicated-only routing with higher per-customer charge.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Might be useful to talk to SRE@east to confirm what our actual cold-start penalty is (token latency + p95 tail).
- Check whether current billing exports include per-GPU-hour granularity for Dec–Feb. If not, request.

Post-meeting follow-up template (copyable):
- Subject: Recap + next steps: Dedicated capacity baseline discussion
- Body: Thanks for time. Recap agreements: baseline 40 GPUs (12 mo), burst credits 20% cap, follow-ups: finance to share unit numbers by 2026-03-09, SRE to validate cold-start delta by 2026-03-07. Meeting owner: Aisha.

Tone reminders for negotiation:
- Be collaborative but firm. Finance needs clear ROI lines (ops cost reduction + SLA avoidance).
- Keep language concrete: call out token throughput numbers rather than vague growth percentages.

—— end of scratchpad ——

Random quick calc log (for my brain):
- If baseline = 40 GPUs at $6k/mo -> $240k/mo -> annual $2.88M.
- If we instead did 24 GPUs (bare minimum) -> $144k/mo -> gap vs demand on a 4x spike = massive. Use this when they ask for lower counts.

Local references (quick links I will pull in):
- Feb traffic export: s3://redwood-ops/logs/ingress/2026-02.csv
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812 (autoscale primer)
- Notes: confluence/redwood/dedicated-capacity-playbook
